small_guidance:
- The current kernel only fuses maxpool+mean+clamp; the ConvTranspose3d still runs via cuDNN and dominates the 19.4 ms. Tuning BLOCK/num_warps further on the tail kernel cannot close the gap to baseline 9.05 ms — the headroom is in the conv-T itself.
- If keeping the tail kernel, autotune over BLOCK ∈ {256, 512, 1024} × num_warps ∈ {4, 8} × num_stages ∈ {2, 3}; pooled_total here is small (8·16·16 = 2048) so BLOCK=512 with num_warps=4 is likely better than 2048/8.
- Switch the conv-T output to channels_last (NDHWC) so the tail kernel's reduction over (D,H,W) per (N,C) is contiguous; current NCDHW already is for fixed (n,c) so this is minor — focus on conv-T.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, ID·IH·IW tile)`, computing the input×weight outer product and scattering into the output grid using `od = id*stride - padding + kd` index math, with atomic adds across IC. This eliminates the cuDNN call that is the runtime bottleneck.
- Alternatively (and simpler given small IC=3, OC=16, kernel=3³=27): implement conv-T as a gather-style direct kernel where each program computes a tile of output `(N, OC, OD·OH·OW)` by iterating kd,kh,kw and gathering the matching input element when `(od+padding-kd) % stride == 0`. Fuse scale + maxpool (kernel=2) + global-avg + clamp into the epilogue of this single kernel — one program per `(N, OC)` reducing across the pooled grid eliminates the intermediate (N,16,33,65,65) tensor entirely.
- The conv-T output is huge (~128·16·33·65·65·4B ≈ 1.1 GB) and is read once by maxpool then thrown away — never materializing it via end-to-end fusion is the dominant win. Persist accumulators in registers per (n,oc) and stream pooled windows.
